Server Configuration Files - Official HumanitZ Wiki
How to Use RCON Commands on a HumanitZ Server
humanitz-bot - Discord bot driving HumanitZ over RCON
How to ban players from joining your HumanitZ server

notes: RCON is a modified Valve Source RCON: the humanitz-bot source notes response request_id is always 0, the server never answers an empty packet (so the usual end-marker trick for multi-packet reads does not work), auth replies with RESPONSE_VALUE before AUTH_RESPONSE, and every command takes roughly 3 seconds to answer. Budget a generous timeout. RCON is TCP on RConPort (default 8888, confirmed on the wiki's Port Forwarding page as '8888 - TCP (RCON Port)') and the wiki calls it mandatory for now - disabling it breaks query/ping. The keys are RCONEnabled=false, RConPort=8888 and RCONPass= in GameServerSettings.ini; the wiki documents the shipped template under the name REF_GameServerSettings.ini. The RCON command names are case-insensitive in practice but are written here with the wiki's casing ('Players' capitalised, 'kick'/'ban'/'unban' lower case). Broadcast is 'admin <message>', which prints to everyone's chat with an [Admin] tag; there is no 'say'. There is no MOTD command - the greeting lives in WelcomeMessage.txt. 'fetchbanned' prints the current ban list and 'sendadminmsgto <SteamID> <message>' whispers one player; neither has a schema field here. Kick and ban take the 17-digit Steam ID (NET ID), NOT a player name; ban also writes the ID into F_BannedPlayers.txt, one unique Steam ID per line. PLAYERS REPLY FORMAT (corrected on review): the official wiki and BisectHosting describe the reply only as 'name/SteamID' and print no sample, but the humanitz-bot RCON service parses each row with '^(.+?) \((\d+)_\+_\|([a-f0-9]+)\)' - player name, a space, then a parenthesised group holding the Steam64 ID, the literal separator '_+_|' and an EOS Product User ID in hex, optionally followed by 'Lv:X', 'Clan:Name' and 'DPassed:X' suffixes. playerParse now follows that working implementation; the previous slash-separated 'name/SteamID' regex would never have matched a real reply. DISAGREEMENT: supercraft.host documents an in-game chat command '/kick [Player]' that takes a player NAME; the official wiki's admin chat-command list contains no /kick at all, so that form is treated as unconfirmed and the RCON Steam-ID form is used.
